description: LLM-powered meeting recap system that produces a single Hierarchical recap view: topically-coherent chapters generated by paper-1's *Ours (full)* method (utterance-pair NSP-BERT coherence scoring + TextTiling sliding-window depth-score cutoffs), with chunked 3rd-person rolling summaries and deBERTa-generated chapter titles from paper-2 §3.2.2. Pipeline is streaming end-to-end (SSE for HTTP, NDJSON for CLI) so the user sees chapter cards as soon as TextTiling confirms a boundary, before the deBERTa title model returns. Highlights pipeline (DR1) is explicitly out of scope per design decision 2026-07-05.
data_corpus_note: data/eval_vi/ contains Vietnamese-translated versions of paper-1's English test sets (dialseg_711, doc2dial), paper-2's AMI/ICSI meeting corpora (meeting_ami, meeting_icsi), plus the project's own meeting_committee sample and tiage. ZYS (Chinese) is NOT shipped with this repo -- the eval-001 feature must source it externally if Chinese segmentation is in scope.

rules.merged_features_share_area: When multiple feature IDs are merged (e.g. svc-001+002), the resulting feature inherits the area of the dominant feature (the first ID). Sub-modules may live in different files but they all belong to the merged feature.
rules.streaming_features_carry_event_contract: Any feature with '+streaming' suffix must reference the canonical event contract in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-05-streaming-hierarchical-recap-design.md Section 6 and emit events in the documented order.

known_gaps.gap: The VibERT NSP checkpoint at vibert_checkpoints_vi/cpt_4000.pth is a user-fine-tuned partial checkpoint (4,000 of 36,000 planned steps; validation accuracy 0.7752 at step 4,000). It matches paper-1 *Ours (full)* architecture but is not at full convergence. Future work (svc-009-extended-finetune) can resume training.

MVP UI uses MockLLMBackbone for chunk rolling summaries and chapter titles. When the real deBERTa checkpoint is wired in, chunk inference latency (~100-500 ms each) may exceed the 1-second UX threshold and require chunk-summary events to become deferred too (currently only titles are deferred per spec D5).

features.title: Topic Segmentation Pipeline (NSP-BERT CoherenceScorer + TextTiling, paper-1 *Ours (full)*)
features.merge_rationale: TextTilingService (svc-002) is a hard consumer of CoherenceScorer (svc-001); splitting forces a stub scorer and double verification for a single coupled pipeline. Both are ported from references_code/dialogue-topic-segmenter (paper-1 reference impl) and share the same checkpoint.
features.user_visible_behavior: CoherenceScorer.score_pair(utt_i, utt_i_plus_1) returns a float in [0, 1] using the fine-tuned NSP-BERT model from paper-1 *Ours (full)* (cross-encoder BERT_base 12L/12H/768, marginal ranking loss η=1, dialog-flow + dialog-topic negative sampling). TextTilingService consumes a score stream, computes depth scores 0.5*(hl+hr-2*s[i]), and emits SegmentEvents when depth_score > τ (τ = μ - σ/2). Sliding window params (window=30, stride=10) come from TextTilingConfig (config-001+).

Boundaries are non-overlapping, strictly increasing, and cover [0, n).

features.notes: Architectural note: paper-1 *Ours (full)* beats every baseline on every metric (P_k=26.80/45.23, F1=0.776/0.660 on DialSeg_711/Doc2Dial — see docs/papers/improving-unsupervised-dialogue-topic-segmentation.md Table 4). The user's checkpoint vibert_checkpoints_vi/cpt_4000.pth is a partial fine-tuning (4k/36k steps, val_acc 0.7752) of this architecture with bert-base-multilingual-cased backbone instead of aws-ai/dse-bert-base; model-002's _coerce_token_ids + embedding resize handle the vocab mismatch (multilingual 119547 vs checkpoint 38168). The neural_texttiling.py code is ported verbatim for the depth_score and boundaries_to_segments functions; the encoder call goes through our CoherenceScorer (mode CM) rather than the paper's segment.py to keep a single code path.

features.title: StreamingOrchestrator: End-to-End Meeting Recap with 6 Event Types
features.merge_rationale: The orchestrator now owns the streaming entry point. Splitting orchestrator into batch + streaming would duplicate meeting_id lifecycle and processing_time_ms; instead, expose a single StreamingOrchestrator that yields incremental state changes.
features.user_visible_behavior: StreamingOrchestrator.process_stream(transcript_iterator) is an async generator that yields 6 event types in the documented order: utterance-accepted, depth-score-updated, segment-closed, chunk-closed, title-emitted, meeting-completed. Title inference is deferred (background asyncio task) so segment cards appear before the deBERTa title returns; chunk summaries are synchronous (final text in the chunk-closed payload). The original batch entry point process_batch remains for offline CLI use.

features.notes: Why SSE not WebSocket: SSE is HTTP, works through corporate proxies, has built-in reconnect via EventSource, and is sufficient because the recap is unidirectional. The end-to-end design is streaming-capable in the orchestrator, so a future 'live ASR' feature can be added by either (a) a WebSocket route that ingests utterances and pipes them into StreamingOrchestrator.process_stream, or (b) HTTP chunked-transfer on the POST body. Both are no-ops in the orchestrator; they only change the transport adapter.
